When Splatoon came out for the Wii U in 2015, playing it really felt like you were a part of something special. With your purchase of that first game, you weren’t just taking a gamble on a new franchise, you were supporting Nintendo in one of their darkest hours. I hadn’t watched any trailers for Splatoon before purchasing it. I laid down my pre-order with blind faith that one of my favorite companies wouldn’t let me down, and they didn’t. Once I started Splatoon, I was hooked. I ended up playing that game every single day for over a year. It made for one of the most fun and memorable summers of my life. 2015 feels like so long ago now, and though Splatoon 2 and 3 have both been great, neither of them will ever be able to recapture the magic that Splatoon introduced.

I’ve been thinking about a project for both the Switch 1 and a possible Switch 2, something that could help bring back the Donkey Kong Country franchise in a big way. Right now, the series is mostly remembered from the Super Nintendo era, with more recent releases like Donkey Kong Country Returns HD and Tropical Freeze.
So my idea would be for you to create HD remakes of the original Super Nintendo games — Donkey Kong Country 1, 2, and 3 — similar to what you did with Donkey Kong Country Returns HD and Tropical Freeze.
After that, I think it would be really cool to develop a brand-new game, something more ambitious. For example, you could bring back different villains from the series, like King K. Rool and the enemies from Returns and Tropical Freeze, and have them work together in a new story to defeat the Kongs from the original games.
I also had the idea of bringing back the rabbit-like enemies from Tropical Freeze and Returns, and mixing all these characters together into one big project.
Another thing I was thinking about is how SEGA made Sonic Mania by working with fans. Maybe you could invite some fans to help develop this project too. I would be very grateful and excited if something like that happened.
I really want to see remakes of the classic Donkey Kong Country games for the Switch, beyond the Nintendo Switch Online versions, since those are just emulations.
I believe this kind of project could be something very new, exciting, and meaningful for the franchise.
Thank you very much for your attention!

The whole keycard thing on the new Switch 2 feels like a huge step backwards for consumers. We're going from owning full physical games to basically having access keys that depend on servers, and that’s not preserving the format or respecting players at all.

It feels like Nintendo just doesn’t care as long as the numbers look good. But I think they’re wrong — if they released full versions on cartridges, they would sell more and still make the same money, if not more. People actually value owning the complete game, not some conditional access.

Personally — and I know I’m not the only one — I won’t be buying any keycard games. Just look at Cyberpunk 2077: when the product is complete, people show up and buy it.

At the end of the day, everyone can do whatever they want with their money, but I’m not paying for a piece of plastic that could become useless the moment they decide to shut down servers.

BREAKING NEWS:  Bean Beasts Actually Failed Experiment, Good Game, Though :3

Sometimes the original concept doesn't perform well in its original intention.  That doesn't equate to total failure, though.

Bean Beasts actually had a much different intent in mind when first conceived: to put a stop to the rampages of Nintendo of Japan's President Shuntaro Furukawa (maturity age 2).

The fully grown president had kicked shins, peed everywhere, and screamed out more than just Nintendo alone.  No longer willing to wait for Nintendo to reign in the infantile Shuntaro Furukawa, Indie Dev Anxious Noob tried to take things into their own hands.  Inspired by Pocketpair's Palworld, Digimon, the Shin Megami Tensei series, and maybe a couple others that were of much higher qulaity than Nintendo's more recent pokemon slop, they tried to train several creatures to lure Shuntaro Furukawa into a series of mazes and run him around until he was too tired to hurt anybody.

The initial tests were a disaster.  Shuntaro Furukawa was chasing down a few innocent civilians while holding out one of his Palworld plushies and shouting, "POKEMON!  MINE!" when he stumbled into the prototype maze.  As soon as he laid eyes on the Bean Beasts, the president again shouted, "POKEMON!  MINE!" before grabbing them up.

Then he tried to eat them raw.

He tried to heat them raw and live.

Apparently, according to one of the Onion's news stories, pokemon were very tasty so he tried to eat them live and raw.  The end result was to grotesque to mention...

Afterwards, Anxious Noob realized that Bean Beasts could actually be a good game concept and released the finished product on Steam on August 21, 2025.  Several months later, Nintendo devs trying to recover from the catastrophic data loss due to Shuntaro Furukawa peeing on their servers tried to use Bean Beasts as a distraction of their own...

If you're reading this and haven't played this game yet but are interested, I'll tell you... 

This game is great! If you like beat 'em ups and the Scott Pilgrim franchise in general, you'll definitely love this game. It's a lot of fun, especially with friends or family.

It was clearly a game made with a lot of care, both in terms of animations, scenery, details, references, and soundtrack.

Even if you're not a Scott Pilgrim fan, this game might be great for you, as it's a love letter to various classic retro games and nerd culture in general, so it has many references and tributes that are fun to notice, also, the game's dialogues are charismatic and funny, which is great for experiencing both alone and with friends. 

Regarding gameplay, those who played the previous Scott Pilgrim game might miss the mechanic of learning new moves and abilities during the game, but overall, I guarantee that won't be a problem, because the item customization and the variety of shops the game has will give you several additions for your characters, and all the available moves for the characters give you a good amount of freedom to play like a fighting game, inventing your own combos using your creativity, so it doesn't get repetitive.

(But remember that this only applies to the characters: Roxie, Ramona, and Gideon. Who are the ones I played with the most. The other characters may have a worse gameplay loop, but I can't comment on that since I haven't tested them yet.)

One very interesting thing to mention about this game is that it has a mechanic where you can drop health or coins to your partner, which makes cooperation in the game much better, since whoever plays better can give more health to the friend in need, or when they need money to buy something in a store, they can combine the money that they both have, to buy it, dropping the money for whoever needs it.

There are several systems in this game that, although not created exclusively for it and already existing in other games, are very well implemented here, and I would love to mention them, but the comment would become too long and YouTube could take it down, so I'll add that extra information in the comment reply for anyone who's interested.

Overall, I highly recommend the game; it's very fun and made with care, and it will certainly be great fun for fans of the franchise or for anyone who wants something to play with friends or family in general.

Pastel colours, bland boring safe artstyles, cringe tumblr-written stories in some cases, and gameplay that just does nothing for me whatsoever and is nigh indistinguishable from the mountains of other similar games released in the past 10 years. The only game I even felt anything for that wasn't immediate dismissal was Ratatan, which I've already known about for years now. 

With how bad both the Partner Showcase and this was, I REALLY hope Nintendo's saving the actual good announcements for their next Nintendo Direct.

Those of us who follow the series don’t want invented content or additions that have nothing to do with the anime or the manga; we want a faithful, official game based on the original story, respecting the material that made the franchise great. I’ve been watching what they’re showing, and there are abilities, mechanics, and additions that never existed, and that ends up ruining the experience for people who truly know and value the work.
I hope they don’t repeat the same old story: release the game, fill their pockets, and then abandon it without caring about the community. If they’re going to do something, do it right—respect the original material and the fans, because decisions like these only end up disappointing the people who genuinely support the franchise and expect a product that lives up to it.

Just finished playing, this game is amazing and dare I say it takes the combat of Paper Mario TTYD and improves on it drastically.
1. you can switch out characters first turn with no punishment and go again. That way, if you are facing an enemy where certain characters have attack advantages, you can throw them out.
2. each character has their own BP. This means you can have each character decked out with their own build. You don't even have to battle with Flynt if you dont want to  and can do two partners instead.
3. the revive mechanic where you use 1 SP to split health with your ally upon their death is amazing. Allows for the bosses/enemies to be able to hit harder without making it feel impossible or as punishing when a partner goes down
4. there is a HARD mode and it is moderately challenging for someone who has played through TTYD probably 10-15 times with various types of runs. I game over'd probably 5 or 6 times total. If you arent stocked with items for the big bosses, its gonna be tough on hard mode.

Game Idea: "The Legend of Zelda: Nexus of Heroes"

Imagine a Zelda game set in a fractured multiverse where different incarnations of Link—from Ocarina's Hero of Time to Breath's Champion—must team up. Each retains their iconic abilities (time manipulation, wolf transformation, Sheikah runes, etc.) to solve collaborative puzzles that no single hero could crack alone.

The goal: rescue the key allies and princesses from their respective eras (Zelda, Midna, Tetra, etc.) to unite against a corruption that has spawned multiple, enhanced versions of Ganon across timelines.

Core gameplay revolves around a temporal hub, strategic hero-swapping for environmental puzzles, and epic multi-phase boss battles requiring perfect synergy between the Links. It’s a celebration of the series' legacy with a fresh, cooperative twist, asking: what if every Hero of Hyrule fought together?

Fun Fact: 
Rayman 2 began development as a 2D platformer. At some point though, Ubisoft decided to turn it into a 3D platformer, but there was problem: they never developed a 3D platformer before. So, the team decided to take a break from Rayman 2 and began working on a side project, which became Tonic Trouble. It was created to test the engine for Rayman 2 and also provided an opportunity for the developers to learn the ropes of 3D game development.

Assunto: Sugestão de Power-Ups para um Novo Jogo do Mario
Olá, equipe Nintendo!
Meu nome é João Victor e sou fã da série Mario desde pequeno. Tenho uma ideia para um novo jogo do Mario, com 5 mundos, 10 fases em cada mundo, e 2 castelos por mundo. A história seria clássica: o Bowser sequestra a Peach e Mario precisa atravessar cada mundo enfrentando Koopas, Links e Bowser Jr., desbloqueando novos power-ups pelo caminho.
Power-Ups sugeridos:
Tigre Pintado – Um power-up laranja com pintas que faz tudo que o Sino de Gato faz, mas 2x mais rápido. Também possui um rugido que derrota inimigos pequenos, como Goombas e Koopas.
Asa de Fogo – Permite que Mario voe por curtos períodos, mas deixa um rastro de chamas que danifica inimigos próximos.
Escudo da Luz – Mario fica invencível por alguns segundos e reflete projéteis inimigos, como bolas de fogo de Bowser Jr.
Bola Magnética – Permite atrair moedas e power-ups próximos à distância, além de criar um pulso magnético que empurra inimigos.
Fantasma Sorridente – Mario fica invisível por um tempo, podendo atravessar inimigos e paredes, e assusta inimigos ao se aproximar, fazendo-os fugir.
Espero que essa sugestão inspire a criação de algo novo e divertido para os fãs. Obrigado por lerem e considerarem minhas ideias!
Atenciosamente,
João Victor
🇺🇸 English (USA)
Subject: Power-Up Suggestions for a New Mario Game
Hello Nintendo Team!
My name is João Victor and I’ve been a Mario fan since I was a child. I have an idea for a new Mario game with 5 worlds, 10 levels per world, and 2 castles per world. The story would be classic: Bowser kidnaps Peach, and Mario must go through each world facing Koopas, Links, and Bowser Jr., unlocking new power-ups along the way.
Suggested Power-Ups:
Spotted Tiger – An orange power-up with spots that does everything the Cat Bell does, but 2x faster. It also has a roar that defeats small enemies like Goombas and Koopas.
Fire Wings – Allows Mario to fly short distances, leaving a trail of fire that damages nearby enemies.
Light Shield – Mario becomes invincible for a few seconds and reflects enemy projectiles, like Bowser Jr.’s fireballs.
Magnetic Ball – Attracts coins and nearby power-ups, and creates a magnetic pulse that pushes enemies away.
Smiling Ghost – Mario becomes invisible for a time, can pass through enemies and walls, and scares enemies when near, making them run away.
I hope this suggestion inspires the creation of something new and fun for Mario fans. Thank you for reading and considering my ideas!
Sincerely,
João Victor

Here's an interesting Easter egg from the latest GB update.
If you start it up, it used to play the classic Game Boy chime sound. Now if you start it up, the coin from Super Mario Land plays.
If you hold the analog stick in any direction like in the GBA app, you can get the classic Game Boy boot sequence to play, complete with the classic chime.
If you have your filter set to the original Game Boy in the settings, the original Game Boy boot logo starts up, but if you have the Game Boy Pocket or Color filters selected, their respective boot sequences start up instead.

Been playing it for a couple of days on Switch OLED, can recommend - actually a pretty fun and chill game about demonic school teenagers set in 90s with nice retro visuals, unique style and music.
Combat is engaging, but can feel a bit repetitive - it's a turn-based, strategic 4-member battle and your score is rated A-C (though I found that scoring A is not that easy since there are tons of combinations and ways how it can go, and you need to find “the one” (the most annoying requirement is probably having to finish after 3 rounds). 
Open world activities are there too - you can do some classics like fishing/karaoke/sides, some raise lvl of friendship with your team members. Parts of the day change, as well as day of the week, you have a calendar of events, so some of the activities can be done each day routinely or each weekend. 
There is a pretty big tree of abilities, which are bought from the shop keeper for opals you receive after each battle, some are unlocked through side quests or other ways. Each team member has a style/element, so you can choose a skill that fits them better and they are interchangeable among them. 
There are some cons too, but most of them come simply from the low budget development and lack of depth in many aspects.

A little disappointing that the Switch 2 version is mostly just a better version of the Switch version (which is based on 7th gen consoles) instead of being its own unique version that was closer to other (at least 8th gen) systems, but I’m still really glad this game has finally come to Switch at all, and glad it seems to be, from what I’ve seen already online, that it’s an okay port and the Switch 2 one has at least a solid 60fps. Plus definitely love that it comes with all the DLC without having to pay for that extra, and love that it’s on $19.99 with a launch discount only making it $17.99. To me, those few things make this much more appealing, and even though it might not be based on the 8th gen version, it still makes it a great way to play this game for people who haven’t yet, and for people who want to take the game on the Go, but doesn’t have anything but a Switch or Switch 2 in that regard. Really a smart move for them for what the game is giving us! 😁

(Okay, Edit: Apparently some of the control options also don’t work properly at this current moment in time, which is really a shame, disappointment, and problem with the game. However, there is always the possibility of them fixing these issues over time, so I’m not too worried about it being a dealbreaker in the long run, just a real problem right now, but the kind that can be fixed if they actually care to. So while disappointing, it can hopefully get sorted out some time soon. But this is a real problem, and one that does hurt accessibility for other people)

8:05 A triumvirate of fofofo, FTWin, and Milky Way has formed. (According to Nep2ne of Big Fat Sea Cows, Five, which I put in the triumvirate last week, is no longer competing.) All three teams have each won two of the six weeks and finished at least 4th every week it has participated. Unless something drastic were to happen, these are the three favorites to win the Playoffs. The team that finishes the regular season in 1st place overall would earn the #1 seed and likely have the least arduous path to Winners Final in the Playoffs, not having to face one of its other titans until then.

Fofofo's spot is all but secure, having finished 1st twice, 2nd once, and 4th twice. If it wanted to go for 1st in the standings, it can still improve its standing by finishing 3rd or better in at least one of the two remaining weeks.

FTWin has two 1sts and two 2nds, incidentally having defeated both fofofo and Milky Way in Grand Finals once apiece and lost to both of them in Grand Finals once apiece via Bracket Resets. It still has one week in hand—one more week to play to complete the minimum five weeks, and finishing either of the two remaining weeks with a win will assure it of at least a top-two seed.

Milky Way has two 1sts and a 2nd and, thus, is compelled to compete in both remaining weeks for a chance at the #1 seed. I noticed its name among the participating teams for this week on Battlefy. While Playoff qualification is possible with only one more result, Milky Way would likely prefer to enter both final weeks to avoid an early encounter with either fofofo or FTWin in the first round of the Playoffs.

Just below the triumvirate of fofofo, FTWin, and Milky Way are a few teams jostling for the 4th and 5th seeds: Duck Motif (360 points/5+ weeks of play), Moonlight (310/4), BEt (280/4), and Gourmet Race (275/4). Assuming that the big three occupy the top three seeds, each of the teams below them would prefer to finish at least 5th to avoid a first round matchup with one of the big three (and likely drop to Loser's Bracket early).

Duck Motif is in a tricky spot. While it is currently in third, this will likely change once Milky Way competes in this upcoming week. Duck Motif also has completed the bare minimum five weeks, so the only way it can improve its Season Standing is to finish one of the two remaining weeks better than tied for 7th (65 points)—its fifth-best finish back in Week 2. However, finishing tied for 5th (70 points) or 4th (75 points) would only add five or ten more points to its standing. Finishing at least 3rd (85 points) once will secure an additional 20 points to its standing and better secure it a top-five seed. It is expected to compete this upcoming week, but it also is the most prominent team to have competed in every week, so fatigue might be a factor. It would be worthwhile to pay attention to how far it goes.

Moonlight, also competing this week, has a simpler task. Unlike Duck Motif, Moonlight has finished in 3rd (twice) and has a week in hand, so finishing at least tied for 5th will add 70 points for a five-week total of 380 points, which should be safe for top five.

BEt exploded onto the scene in Week 3 with a 2nd place finish but has struggled to compete consistently enough since then. Also slated to play this week, it would have to also compete next week as well to replace the (relatively) poor showing in Week 5. To have a realistic chance at a top-five seed, BEt would have to finish at least 3rd once and at least tied for 5th another week.

Gourmet Race has been steadily improving every week it has entered. As of this writing, it is not yet listed to compete on Battlefy. If it does not compete this week, a top five spot might be out of reach, but its chances to reach the Playoffs (if it were to compete and finish well enough–at least tied for 5th–in the final week) should be good.

Finally, below those teams are the few grasping for the final spots. Triggerfish Zones Supremacy (TZS) is in a similar spot as Duck Motif. Having already played in at least five weeks, it can only improve its standing with better results. Healthy diet food groups has a week in hand and can easily leapfrog TZS with a good showing this week.

One more team to pay attention to this week is Hypernova. Unfortunately, according to team member Synapse, it underwent a mid-season roster change, meaning that, by rule, its Season Standings had to start from zero. However, it can and will spoil another team's playoff push if given the opportunity. It might not make the Playoffs, but it will likely influence which teams will.

Past and new courses, loads of songs, lots of modes and ways to play, goals and achievements, collectibles, machine customizations,  a market for your customizations, character wear, loads of cute additions like the gummy stuff and license card, story with so much lore references, no DLC, plus so much more that I'm sure I forgot to mention because we were just spoiled with so much content info!!

But then, this game was announced and I was hyped until I came to a realization that the game will only take place within the Lumiose City. Didn't gave it much thought at first until the 1st gameplay reveal where I feel like the setting within the city only was very limited. The one thing I love about Legends Arceus was that while that game isn't technically an open-world, the areas still felt huge for exploration and I really like exploring them. This game feels like the opposite of it and I do feel like the buildings looking dull and the lack of NPC (plus, buildings that you cannot enter expect maybe some few) doesn't help.

But probably the worst aspect for me is locking the Megas of the Kalos starters (Greninja, Delphox and Chesnaught) in an online match and as someone who isn't into competitive battles, I feel like I'm being punished for it. I was excited when they got announced, only to be slapped in the face by telling us that their Megas can only be obtained through online battles. I would love to use Mega Greninja and Mega Delphox while I go through the story but locking them on an online match made it impossible to do so. 

I really want to be excited for this game and who knows, maybe I could end up enjoying it when it launches but right now, I feel very upset about the decisions made on this game.

Few things I noticed that stood out (also added stuff that others in the comments have added):

This game involves 4 different stories with 4 different protagonists.

It was literally said to our face at the end of the direct: “This intertwining story happens alongside our favorite games.”

The four characters shown; Cai, Theodora, Dietrich, Leda; might collectively be the 4 protagonists of the game. Not sure if there will be 4 separate routes akin to Three Houses, or if it’s going to “weave” together 4 chapters into one story like Radiant Dawn. 

This might be the first mainline game in a while (that isn’t a remake) where we don’t have an Avatar.

Reason why this may be true is because all 4 units have access to a “storage” mechanic which is generally reserved only for lords or protagonists in previous games.
Also, notice how none of them make contact with each other in the trailer (edit: I stand corrected there is dietrich but as a “green ally” in the battle map with Cai).

It’s too early to know since they were the only units showcased, but it’s possible that their ability “Blaze Arts” is unique to them due to a connection to the “Crest of Flames”, i.e., Sothis. Maybe this is the power that Cai displays from his hand but doesn’t have a crest associated with it.

Dietrich is a myrmidon but level 37, which is pretty wild for a base level class(unless it’s separate and unique to him in this game). All the other characters shown were 13/18/20 (as someone pointed out this could be modified just for the trailer like in a previous trailer for engage)

Answerer: “a magic sword counted among the Hero’s Relics”
His special skill, murderous intent, is a direct callback to jeritza / death knight.
